question: Should AG-UI be accepted as a bundled OpenClaw channel with new HTTP endpoints and dependencies, or should it be delivered as an externally installed official plugin until a broader external-channel policy is settled?
rationale: The patch is a new product and security boundary, not a mechanically established regression fix; repository policy favors lean core/plugin ownership, while the discussion raises an unresolved channel-bundling precedent.

options.title: Pause for ownership and security approval
options.body: Do not merge this branch until the channel ownership model and the exact dependency graph are explicitly approved for this head.

options.title: Sponsor a bundled channel
options.body: Accept AG-UI as a bundled channel, then require security approval, documented route/auth defaults, and redacted live end-to-end evidence before merge.

options.title: Move it to an external package
options.body: Keep the AG-UI implementation as an independently installed official plugin and identify any genuinely missing core seam in a separate, narrow proposal.

recommendation.title: Pause for ownership and security approval
recommendation.body: Do not merge this branch until the channel ownership model and the exact dependency graph are explicitly approved for this head.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the original implementation and the most detailed currently visible rationale about the bundled-channel boundary, though a repository owner must make the final product decision.
